crossRefs.note: “For truly, both Herod and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles and the people of Israel, were gathered together against…
to do whatever your hand and your council foreordained to happen.
Having blindfolded him, they struck him on the face and asked him, “Prophesy! Who is the one who struck you?”
They spoke many other things against him, insulting him.
But I am a worm, and no man; a reproach of men, and despised by the people.
You know my reproach, my shame, and my dishonor. My adversaries are all before you.
Reproach has broken my heart, and I am full of heaviness. I looked for some to take pity, but there was none; for…
Yahweh, the Redeemer of Israel, and his Holy One, says to him whom man despises, to him whom the nation abhors, to a…
He was despised and rejected by men, a man of suffering and acquainted with disease. He was despised as one from whom…
Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the Praetorium, and gathered the whole garrison together against him.
He said to them, “Elijah indeed comes first, and restores all things. How is it written about the Son of Man, that he…
The soldiers led him away within the court, which is the Praetorium; and they called together the whole cohort.
Jesus therefore came out, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple garment. Pilate said to them, “Behold, the man!”

people.name: Herod
people.line: Tetrarch of Galilee during Jesus' ministry.

people.name: Pilate
people.line: Roman governor who presided over Jesus' trial

translations.web: Herod with his soldiers humiliated him and mocked him. Dressing him in luxurious clothing, they sent him back to Pilate.
translations.bsb: And even Herod and his soldiers ridiculed and mocked Him. Dressing Him in a fine robe, they sent Him back to Pilate.
translations.kjv: And Herod with his men of war set him at nought, and mocked him, and arrayed him in a gorgeous robe, and sent him again to Pilate.
translations.asv: And Herod with his soldiers set him at nought, and mocked him, and arraying him in gorgeous apparel sent him back to Pilate.
